requirements.note: Inset-grouped list grouped by month, newest first. Each row shows name, date, exercise count and volume. Volume is rounded to whole pounds (6,768 for 6,767.5).
Detail has a summary section (date, exercises, sets, total volume), then one section per exercise listing its sets with a per-exercise volume footer. Exercise rows push to the exercise screen.

Inline name field. Multi-select picker with a search field (proper 'No Results' state) and muscle filter chips. Add Set sheet uses a number pad, +/- buttons and prefills from the last set. Tapping a set edits it, and the edit sheet has Delete Set. Swipe-to-delete works and volume updates. Finish shows a confirmation popover that notes exercises with no sets will be dropped, then switches to History and pushes the new workout.
Library tab lists all exercises grouped by muscle, with a search field in the navigation bar.
Shows muscle and equipment, the best set (72.5 lb × 14, linked to its workout) and every workout the exercise appears in, with a count footer.
After relaunch the in-progress workout comes back with its sets, the timer and the selected tab. The finished workout is still in History after relaunch.

bugs: On the exercise screen opened from a workout, that workout's row stays highlighted in grey (the selection never clears).
tells: The reps and weight steppers are hand-drawn round −/+ buttons, not UIStepper. At the largest text size the − and + buttons are different sizes.
The weight field starts with a literal '0' rather than a placeholder, so typing 135 gives '0135'. The next set's sheet is prefilled, so typing appends to the old value.
The Library tab uses a small inline title while History and Workout use large titles.
History volumes are rounded to whole pounds, so the half-pound precision in the data is hidden.
A.scroll: History and Library scroll like native lists: momentum, no blank or popping rows, the large title collapses, rubber-banding works at the top, and scroll position is kept after pushing a detail and coming back.

requirements.note: Inset-grouped list grouped by month, newest first. Each row shows name, full date, exercise count and exact volume (6,767.5 lb). A 'Workout in Progress' resume row appears at the top when one exists.
Summary section (date, exercises, sets, volume), then a section per exercise listing its sets. Exercise rows push to the exercise screen.

A name sheet (with suggestions) starts the workout. The picker has a bottom search field and a muscle pop-up menu. It is single-select, so each exercise needs its own trip. The Add Set sheet uses a decimal pad and prefills from the last set. Tapping a set edits it (the sheet has Delete Set), and swipe-to-delete works. Finish adds the workout to History straight away, with no confirmation.
Exercises tab lists the library grouped by muscle, with a search field that appears when you pull down.
Best set appears prominently (72.5 lb × 14, with a note on how ties are broken), above muscle, equipment and a 'Workouts (4)' list of linked rows.
After relaunch the in-progress workout is restored, with a resume row in History. The finished workout is still there after relaunch.

tells: The 'No Workout in Progress' empty state is hand-built: its title is regular weight rather than the bold ContentUnavailableView style.
The Add Set sheet is prefilled, so typing appends to the old value (95 becomes 95100) instead of replacing it.
The exercise picker is single-select, so adding several exercises means opening the sheet several times.
Finish commits immediately with no confirmation, which makes an accidental tap easy.
B.scroll: History and Exercises scroll like native lists: smooth momentum, the large title collapses, the search field appears on pull-down, no row popping, and scroll position is kept on returning from a detail.

why: Both apps meet every requirement, persist correctly and look like native iOS 26-style apps in light, dark and at the largest text size. A's workout flow is richer: a multi-select picker with filter chips and a no-results state, prefilled steppers, best-set hints while logging, and a confirm-on-finish popover that warns about exercises with no sets. B is slightly cleaner in places (exact volumes, no stuck highlight) but its logging flow is clunkier.
